summary: Recorded the newterm receipt and broadened the defect's trigger. Receipt 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 (all four tests passed) showed that a follower which merely re-promises in a new term created by an ordinary leader change — with no reconnected() call at all — ends at accepted 7 over its six indices of content, with its reconfiguration endpoint flipped to false, its StopSign index read (5) returning None, index 6 returning the StopSign and its decided-log read from 0 returning nothing (event 11), while the new leader and the node that received no message stayed at 6/6 (events 9, 10) and the pre-change baseline held for all three (events 6-8). The declared result comparisons on that follower (accepted index bound, decided index bound, StopSign at index 5, six-element decided read) were violated at index 11; the leader-side comparisons held at index 9 and the cut-off node's at index 10. The trigger is therefore the resume point covering the StopSign, not the reconnection API. Updates: the interpretation now covers all three receipts separately with same-run controls and joint_history (violated/asserted), the four knowledge records are re-conditioned on the observed producer paths (same-run resync, single resync, ordinary leader change) with per-receipt execution indices, the open gap's answer distinguishes the witnessed follower half from the still-unexecuted leader-side instance and the sourced snapshot-branch reasoning, and a successor experiment is submitted that unblocks the previously cut-off node and lets it take the lead, sampling a leader whose own decided index becomes the followers' resume point with comparisons on its own accepted index, its StopSign index read, its decided-log read and its decided index. Incomplete: that staleleader execution, a snapshot-enabled run, loss- and timer-triggered re-synchronization, larger clusters, and the internal accepted-index vector behind the phantom decision.
